For buyers · Kenya

Working with AfriScan in Kenya: notes for procurement teams

What the e-GP system, the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, the drone rules and the Data Protection Act mean when a public body, a state corporation or a private asset owner in Kenya buys structure mapping, wayleave registers or drone work, and what to ask any supplier for. A summary of public rules as of 27 September 2026, for orientation; it is not legal or tax advice.

Send tender documents How we work

In short

Five questions every supplier file should answer

How bids are submitted

Through e-GP, on paper, or both? Follow the submission instructions in each tender.

Citizen preferences

Is the tender reserved for or weighted towards citizens, and, for an international tender, how does a foreign tenderer meet the 40 per cent citizen-sourcing rule?

Drone work

If the scope includes drone work, which Kenyan company will fly it, and do its KCAA certificate, security clearances and job authorisations cover the task?

Personal data

Who is controller and who is processor, what does the processor contract say, and which sub-processors does the work rely on?

Imagery

Which imagery will the work use, with which capture dates and licence terms, and does the buyer already hold any of it?

Electronic procurement

The e-GP system

Public procurement in Kenya is moving onto the e-GP system. The Public Procurement Regulatory Authority describes bidding, evaluation and awards moving “entirely online”.

The Treasury Cabinet Secretary told the Senate that mandatory use took effect on 1 July 2025, with 1,543 procuring entities onboarded, 9,772 tenders published and 2,604 contracts processed (KBC, 17 June 2026). In September 2025 the High Court issued conservatory orders requiring manual and electronic bids to be accepted equally until a hearing (KBC, 8 September 2025). Read the submission instructions in each tender.

State corporations and utilities also run their own supplier registration and prequalification alongside e-GP, and lender-financed programmes follow their lender’s procurement rules, with notices on the World Bank’s projects site for the programmes it finances.

Where to look

  • e-GP Kenya: tenders from public procuring entities
  • PPRA: the regulator, its guidance and training
  • National Land Commission: compulsory acquisition and wayleave processes
  • Mining Cadastre Portal: mineral-right applications and the public register
  • World Bank projects: notices for programmes it finances

Citizen and local preferences

What section 157 of the PPADA requires

The Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act 2015 (Cap. 412C), as consolidated after the 2022 amendments, sets four rules in section 157 that shape who can win a mapping or drone contract:

  • Exclusive preference for citizens where the funding is wholly from the national government, a county government or a Kenyan body and the amount is below the prescribed threshold (s.157(8)(a)).
  • A margin of preference for local goods and by local shareholding (s.157(8)(b)).
  • The 40 per cent rule: “all foreign tenderers participating in international tenders” must “source at least forty percent of their supplies from citizen contractors prior to submitting a tender” (s.157(9)), as a mandatory preliminary evaluation criterion.
  • Reserved value: at least 30 per cent of procurement value each year goes to youth, women and persons with disability (s.157(10)).

A Local Content Bill 2025 is before Parliament. The President has directed that it be expanded to set a framework for small-scale trade, identifying activities that may be reserved for citizens, while Kenya “remains open to lawful foreign investment, employment and enterprise” (KBC, 8 September 2026). Check its status before each tender.

In a proposal

For a tender that scores these rules, the proposal names the company that will contract, identifies the parts of the work sourced from citizen contractors, and answers each preference criterion in writing, so the evaluation committee can check it against the tender document.

Drone work

Who may fly, and what to ask for

Commercial drone work in Kenya needs an RPAS Operator Certificate from the Kenya Civil Aviation Authority, which it issues only to a company registered in Kenya with its principal place of business there and a security clearance from the Ministry responsible for defence (Civil Aviation (Unmanned Aircraft Systems) Regulations 2025, regs 24 and 26). Everyone who engages in the operations needs a security clearance too (reg 4), every operation needs KCAA authorisation (reg 23), and aerial photography for mapping needs a month’s written notice to the Director of Surveys (Survey Act s.42).

For evaluation, split any scope into its satellite or desk-based part, which needs no aviation approval, and its drone part, which needs all of them. Ask for the flying company’s certificate number, expiry date and operations specifications, its security clearances, its insurance and the notice letter to the Director of Surveys.

Drone surveys are subject to the approvals and security clearances each job requires. Every AfriScan proposal with a drone element names the Kenyan company that will fly it.

The client checklist

Thirteen points to check with any drone operator before the first flight, from the operator certificate and security clearances to the Survey Act notice and the data clause.

Data and imagery

Processor terms and imagery licences

Data Protection Act terms

The Act reaches processors outside Kenya and lists “property details” among sensitive data. The contract should carry the regulation 24 processor terms, the authorisation of sub-processors under regulation 25, and where data is processed and stored.

Read

Imagery licences and credits

Each proposal names the imagery the work will use, its capture dates and its licence terms. Open data is credited as its licence requires, and map-service basemaps are never delivered as survey imagery. See data sources.

What we send

For your supplier file

  • A written proposal: scope, method, imagery plan, deliverables and schedule
  • An imagery statement: sources, capture dates, licence terms and credits
  • For any drone element: the Kenyan company that will fly it, and the approvals its flights need
  • The data terms: controller and processor roles, sub-processors, where data is processed and stored, and for how long
  • Sample outputs, and a redacted sample report on request
  • A statement of which registrations are in place for your contract

Tell us which registrations and certificates your process requires, and the reference of the tender or RFQ. The proposal names the company that will contract and answers each requirement in writing.

We respond to RFQs, tenders and requests for information. Send your supplier or prequalification forms with your request.

Frequently asked questions

What is the 40 per cent rule for foreign tenderers?

Section 157(9) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act requires “all foreign tenderers participating in international tenders” to “source at least forty percent of their supplies from citizen contractors prior to submitting a tender”. It is a mandatory preliminary evaluation criterion, so a bid that does not meet it can fail before the technical evaluation.

Does a satellite mapping contract raise the drone questions?

No. The KCAA operator certificate, the security clearances and the operation authorisation apply only where an aircraft is flown. The Survey Act’s one-month notice speaks of aerial photography for mapping, which satellite imagery arguably is not; if your contract depends on that point, ask counsel. Where a scope includes drone work, the proposal separates it, names the Kenyan company that will fly it and lists the approvals its flights need, so your evaluation can treat each part on its own terms.

Is bidding through e-GP mandatory?

The National Treasury has said that mandatory use of e-GP took effect on 1 July 2025, and PPRA describes bidding, evaluation and awards moving entirely online. In September 2025 the High Court issued conservatory orders requiring manual and electronic bids to be accepted equally pending a hearing. Follow the submission instructions in each tender document.

What do you need from us to prepare a proposal?

The route, network or boundary file, the counties, the wayleave or reserve widths, the dates the record must reflect, the deliverables and the deadline. With a tender, send the documents, the portal and the reference number your process uses. Every proposal is scoped to your route or site.

Which company will contract with us?

The proposal names the company that will contract and the one that will fly any drone work, and states which registrations are in place for your contract, so your supplier file can be checked against your process before award.

Preparing a tender or a supplier file?

Send the tender or RFQ documents, the deadline and your supplier forms. The proposal answers each requirement and states which registrations are in place for your contract.
